subject: Business Models
title: Hotel Franchises
description: A quick, practical guide to Hotel Franchises.

hook.text: Marriott owns 30 hotel brands but operates only 25% of its rooms. Franchisees run the rest.

buildup.text: Hotel owners pay Marriott 5-6% of room revenue plus marketing fees for the brand name and booking system.

discovery.text: Brand affiliation drives bookings. An independent hotel gets 15% of its bookings online; a Marriott gets 65%.

twist.text: Marriott's 'asset-light' strategy means it doesn't own buildings. It earns fees on $23 billion in room sales.

climax.text: Hotel franchising is the most profitable model in hospitality. Own the brand, not the building.

punchline.text: 30 brands, 25% operated directly. Marriott sells its name, not beds.

quiz.question: What percentage of Marriott's rooms are franchised?

details.summary: Hotel franchise systems like Marriott, Hilton, and IHG own very few physical hotels. Instead, they license their brand and reservation systems to independent hotel owners who pay franchise fees and follow brand standards. The brand company earns asset-light fees while owners carry the property risk.
details.whyItMatters: Hotel franchising created an asset-light model worth hundreds of billions. Marriott manages or franchises over 8,000 properties while owning almost none..
takeaways: Major hotel brands own few properties, licensing their names to independent owners
Franchise fees include per-room-night charges, reservation system fees, and marketing dues
Brand and loyalty program access justifies franchise costs through higher occupancy rates

faq.question: How do hotel franchise fees work?
faq.answer: Hotel owners pay an initial fee for the brand license, then ongoing fees of 10 to 15 percent of room revenue covering the franchise royalty, reservation system access, loyalty program participation, and marketing fund contributions. Total fee loads make hotel franchising among the most expensive.

faq.question: Why do hotel owners pay high franchise fees instead of going independent?
faq.answer: Branded hotels achieve 15 to 30 percent higher occupancy through loyalty programs and reservation systems. Business travelers book through corporate programs that only include branded properties. Online booking algorithms favor recognized brands. The revenue premium exceeds the fees.
